summary:
Earth Trend Detectives is an educational climate-science game that combines NASA datasets, 3D exploration, interactive charts and gamification.

Its strongest feature is connecting scientific observations to actual environmental mechanisms rather than simply showing climate statistics.

Its most valuable potential use is in schools, environmental education, science exhibitions and NASA Space Apps Challenge demonstrations.
details:
A third-person 3D detective game built on real NASA Earth observations, plus a website that acts as its mission control: a live Earth globe, case-file charts, a data lab, an educator pack, a leaderboard and a printable certificate. A small Node and SQLite backend stores scores for a shared leaderboard.

Made for the NASA Space Apps Challenge, Challenge 02: Be an Earth System Trend Detective. Not an official NASA product.

Features

  • Game (public/game/index.html): three cases (Arctic sea ice, coral bleaching, Amazon moisture). Explore by jeep and on foot, read three hidden sensors, answer a quiz.
  • Play page: the game in an embedded frame with a control panel (case, agent name, fullscreen, sync, rank, brief, controls).
  • Live Earth: interactive globe with real earthquakes (USGS), wildfires, storms and volcanoes (NASA EONET), and weather on tap (Open-Meteo).
  • Cases, Data lab, NASA data, Educators, Leaderboard, Profile, Certificate, Impact.

Project structure

earth-trend-detectives/
├── package.json
├── .gitignore
├── README.md
├── db/
│ ├── schema.sql tables: players, scores, view: leaderboard
│ └── seed.js optional demo data
├── server/
│ ├── server.js Express app: static site + API
│ └── db.js opens SQLite and applies the schema
└── public/ the website (can also be hosted statically)
├── *.html one file per page
├── assets/css/style.css
├── assets/js/
│ ├── utils.js helpers, font loader, year interpolation
│ ├── data.js chart series, cases, ranks
│ ├── storage.js profile, save codes, scores, API sync
│ ├── bridge.js website <-> game messaging
│ ├── ui.js nav bar, footer, sync dialog
│ ├── globe.js Three.js globe
│ └── pages/ one script per page
└── game/index.html the 3D game (unmodified)

Each page loads the shared scripts in this order: utils, data, storage, bridge, ui, then its own file from pages/.

Run it

Needs Node 20 or newer.

npm install
npm start # http://localhost:3000
npm run seed # optional: add demo players

The SQLite file is created at db/detectives.sqlite on first start and is ignored by git.

Database and API

Method

Route

Purpose

POST

/api/scores

body { agent, caseId, score }, keeps each player's best score per case

GET

/api/leaderboard

top 50 players by total score

GET

/api/players/:agent

one player's scores

Case IDs: arctic_01, coral_02, amazon_03. Scores are 0 to 1000. There are no accounts, so anyone can submit under any name; treat the board as a classroom feature, not a secure ranking.

The site still works without the server (for example on GitHub Pages or Netlify). Scores then stay in the browser, and the leaderboard uses pasted save codes only.

How the site and game talk

  • Both use localStorage key earthDetectiveProfile, format { agent, scores }. Save codes are base64 JSON.
  • The game posts GODOT_CASE_SOLVED and MISSION_COMPLETE messages to its parent page, and the site updates the profile.
  • A case opens with game/index.html?case=arctic_01&agent=Name.

Deploy

  • With the database: any Node host (Render, Railway, Fly.io). Start command npm start. Use a persistent disk or set DB_FILE to a path on it, since free tiers often reset local files.
  • Static only: upload the contents of public/ to Netlify, GitHub Pages or Cloudflare Pages.

Data sources

NASA Earth Observatory Blue Marble: Next Generation imagery (credited to NASA Earth Observatory), NASA GIBS, NASA EONET, NASA POWER, USGS Earthquake Hazards Program, Open-Meteo, NASA GISS GISTEMP, NSIDC Sea Ice Index, NOAA GML, NASA Sea Level Change, INPE PRODES.

Chart values are rounded and interpolated between five-year anchors, and some 2025 values are estimates. They teach the shape of a trend and are not for citation.
